ground_truth_draft.expected_behavior: http1_header_read_timeout now starts immediately when the connection is established (in poll_read_head before parsing), instead of only after the first header bytes arrive in parse_headers. A client that opens a TCP connection and sends nothing is now closed after the configured timeout.
ground_truth_draft.rationale_from_pr_metadata: PR title 'fix(server): start header read timeout immediately' and body 'used to start once there was a single read of headers. This change makes it start the timer immediately, right when the connection is established. Closes #3178'. jeromegn comment: 'hyper is vulnerable to malicious actors who may just open connections and never send anything.' New test header_read_timeout_starts_immediately asserts EOF after timeout with zero bytes sent — anchors the fix as a connection-lifetime/timer-arming ordering change.
